newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO GO SECOND ABOVE BARCELONA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO GO SECOND ABOVE BARCELONA.

text.p: Spanish champions Atletico Madrid lost ground on the leaders after scrambling a hectic 1-1 draw at Athletic Bilbao on Sunday.
But Deportivo Coruna made no mistake and beat Valencia 1-0 to go second above Barcelona.
Deportivo were two points behind Real Madrid and two ahead of Barcelona, who lost 2-0 to their arch-rivals on Saturday.
Atletico stayed fifth but slipped to 10 points adrift of their city neighbours,.

They went ahead at the end of a scrappy first half when Kiko Narvaez controlled a ball in the area and turned beautifully to find Milinko Pantic on the far post, where the Serbian set-piece specialist made no mistake.

Shortly after the break Jose Molina rose superbly to knock a header from Karanka against the bar, and the Atletico keeper had to pull out the stops as Luis Fernandez ordered his men forward in search of the equaliser.
The Athletic coach was rewarded when Joseba Etxeberria levelled with a superb 25-metre strike.
A minute later Atletico lost Radek Bejbl after the Czech midfielder picked up his second yellow card for a reckless challenge.
Deportivo survived a late surge from Valencia after taking an early lead through French midfielder Corentin Martins.
Coach John Toshack was understandably happy with his side's win, but indicated that he will be looking for a new centre-forward when the Spanish transfer market opens next week.
"We played our best first half of the season," said the Welshman, "But we didn't get a good return from it."
Toshack's side were set to meet Barcelona on December 29, but pressure from players resulted in all league fixtures on that day switched to February 19.
The change, together with World Cup qualifiers, means that there will be only one more weekend of league action in Spain this year.
As a result Real will begin 1997 ahead of arch-rivals Barcelona, and need only a draw in next weekend's game at Valladolid to guarantee spending the Christmas break as leaders.
Real Betis, going well in fourth place, could afford to waste a penalty in despatching Logrones 5-1, with two goals from newly-capped midfielder Roberto Rios.
Nigerian forward Christopher Ohen gave himself an early present for his wedding on Monday by scoring the only goal for Compostela at Rayo Vallecano.
The result moved Compostela ahead of Zaragoza, 3-0 losers at Espanyol and already looking relegation-bound.
Just 18 months after winning the European Cup Winners' Cup, Zaragoza are third from bottom.
